findings.reason: a node dispatched with "make a held preflight exit 3 again" will attempt to reverse a deliberate verb retirement or will overwrite the documented exit-10 meaning in the refusal table, so the section sends its node at the wrong mechanism and cannot be closed on the verdict it asserts.
findings.text: §35's Why says a held preflight exits 10 because "Either the verb now exits with an unrelated code, or the hold's exit code moved without the test", but `crew preflight` is a retired verb: `reckon/crew/tombstones.py:151-159` registers it with successor `crew budget --check`, and `TOMBSTONE_EXIT_CODE = 10` (`tombstones.py:37`) is the retirement code documented in the crew group's own help, not the hold's code at all. Running the verb proves it: `CliRunner().invoke(reckon.cli.main, ["crew","preflight","--project","sample"])` returns `{"retired": "preflight", "successor": "crew budget --check", "exit_code": 10}`, exit 10. Both branches of the Deliverable are therefore wrong: "make a held preflight exit 3 again" would require un-retiring a deliberately folded verb, and "update the test and the refusal table to match" 10 would add a row colliding with the code the crew group help already publishes as the retirement code. The correct repair is that the test should drive the successor `crew budget --check` and assert 3 on a held report — which the plan's Deliverable never names

findings.reason: without a control that reaches the successor's exit-code branch the node cannot show its guard fires, and a control that restores the tombstone demonstrates nothing about the code the repair touches.
findings.text: §35's Done-when defines its negative control as "restores the code path found, and the test then fails with `assert 10 == 3` again", but the code path that returns 10 is the tombstone for the retired name; once the test is pointed at the successor `crew budget --check` (the only repair that leaves the retirement intact) the tombstone is never reached, so restoring it cannot make the test fail with `assert 10 == 3`, and the desired 3-vs-other assertion has no declared mutation the head arm fails that the base arm does not
